rationale: Remains Unknown (Researched): No controlled human clinical study (in PD or non-PD), clinical case series, or defensibly transferable animal model isolates ground sesame seed on visual hallucination frequency. Consistent with Round 6 sesame seed claims (0970-1000, where 30 of 31 symptoms remained open and only pain severity 0992 carried minimal_signal easing), human trials of ground sesame paste/ardeh (Mirmiran 2013, PMID:24206407, n=41 T2D) assessed blood lipids rather than neuropsychiatric or psychotic endpoints, and the 2026 sesame systematic review (Zhao 2026, PMID:41391419) documents no clinical hallucination signal. Safety caveats: major IgE-mediated food allergen capable of severe anaphylaxis (~0.1-0.2% prevalence; US FASTER Act 9th major allergen; Zhao 2026, PMID:41391419), colonic sesame seed phytobezoar/obstruction risk with heavy unchewed seed intake (Shaw 2007, PMID:18047637—pertinent in PD slow-transit constipation), pregnancy/emmenagogue uterotonic hazard at medicinal doses (Aghababaei 2021, PMID:34192691), and dietary protein timing considerations if large tahini/seed portions are taken with levodopa.

Remains Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial (PD or non-PD) has evaluated roasted or cooked shiitake mushroom on anxiety severity (unlike Round 5 oyster mushroom, which had a dedicated 12-week human whole-mushroom RCT). Preclinical studies tested purified eritadenine in non-PD mice (Gutierrez-Rodelo 2023, PMID:37541318) and a hydroalcoholic extract in adult zebrafish (Campelo 2025, PMID:41074366)—too remote in both matrix and species for clinical transfer—while human whole-shiitake RCTs measured only immune/lipid biomarkers (Dai 2015 PMID:25866155; Spim 2021 PMID:34375514). Weighting direct null human RCTs over remote supraphysiological/inconsistent preclinical extracts keeps the claim open. Safety & preparation caveats: spinach is the single largest dietary oxalate contributor linked to calcium-oxalate kidney stones and biopsy-proven oxalate nephropathy from heavy raw/smoothie/pureed loads (Taylor 2007 PMID:17538185; Massey 2007 PMID:17604750; Samra 2024 PMID:39310402)—boiling removes 30-87% of soluble oxalate vs 5-53% for steaming (Chai & Liebman 2005 PMID:15826055) and dietary calcium pairing plus hydration reduce absorption; high vitamin K1 interacts with warfarin (Chang 2014 PMID:24383939); and rare anticholinergic weed adulteration (Datura/Mandragora) has occurred in contaminated leafy batches (Caprai 2024; Jimenez-Mejias 1990). Botanical/supplement boundaries: strictly separated from Amaranthus "red spinach" (Townsend 2022 PMID:33754923), isolated spinach thylakoids/Appethyl (Montelius 2014; EFSA 2023), isolated ecdysterone (Isenmann 2019), and supraphysiological synthetic rubiscolin-6.

Minimal directional signal that whole-fruit strawberry supplementation may ease chronic joint pain in non-PD adults, opposing the raw-strawberry worsens hypothesis as Maybe False (50.005). Remains Unknown (Researched): No controlled human clinical study (in PD or non-PD) or transferable preclinical experiment isolates refined sunflower oil on apathy severity. Across neurological, psychiatric, and cardiometabolic RCTs (e.g., Savard 2023 PMC10587967; Lopresti 2026 PMID:42413424; MEMO PMID:18678826), sunflower oil serves routinely as an inert placebo oil comparator rather than an active intervention, and the CAM Care in PD baseline poster found null total PRO-PD symptoms (+2 pts, p=0.787; Mischley 2017). Public PD forum discussions (HealthUnlocked 2025; Parkinson's UK 2026 topic 48604) reflect contrasting opinions on seed oils without clinical apathy severity data. Safety caveats: exogenous lipoid pneumonia aspiration risk if repeatedly given orally or used for oil pulling in dysphagia or reflux (Marangu 2018, PMC6079933); repeatedly overheated/thermally oxidized frying sunflower oil worsened rat memory and motor coordination relative to native oil (Zarei 2021, PMID:33170419; Keremane 2024, PMID:39704875); high calorie density and omega-6/omega-3 fatty-acid balance considerations; while refined sunflower oil is generally tolerated by sunflower-seed-allergic individuals (An 2021, PMC8305662), unrefined cold-pressed oil may carry trace seed proteins.

Remains Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial in Parkinson's disease or non-PD adults—and no isolated preclinical behavioral model—has evaluated cooked culinary Swiss chard (Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris / var. cicla) on anxiety severity. Zero human clinical trials have tested cooked Swiss chard on anxiety severity (and Round 2 beetroot juice cognitive trials strictly do NOT transfer because beetroot root and Swiss chard leaves are biochemically distinct; Almeida 2025 PMID:40006850). The only preclinical behavioral study containing Swiss chard (El-Khodor 2021 PMID:34730480, already local) gavaged a proprietary blend of dried Swiss chard leaf juice + aerial buckwheat plant to magnesium-depleted rats: it CANNOT isolate Swiss chard from buckwheat (attribution_fit=remote/unusable), failed to reverse low-Mg elevated plus-maze anxiety (NULL on anxiety), failed to improve Y-maze spontaneous alternation (p=0.6988, NULL), and showed only a comparator-ambiguous object-recognition difference (p=0.0266). Rat valproic-acid (Tunali 2020 PMID:32754946) and bile-duct-ligation (Ozel 2021 PMID:34173678) brain studies measured biochemical oxidative markers only with ZERO behavioral tests. Safety & botanical boundaries: Swiss chard (Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris / var. cicla leaf/stalk) is strictly separated from beetroot root (B. vulgaris var. conditiva, covered in Round 2; Almeida 2025 PMID:40006850)—beetroot juice nitrate RCTs do NOT transfer; chard leaves carry high soluble oxalate linked to kidney stones and biopsy-proven acute oxalate nephropathy after a large cooked freshly harvested chard meal (Jankowski 2026 PMID:41877053; boiling removes 30-87% soluble oxalate vs steaming 5-53%, Chai & Liebman 2005 PMID:15826055); very high vitamin K1 (~830 ug/100 g) interacts with warfarin (Chang 2014 PMID:24383939); leaves accumulate high nitrate/nitrite (Iammarino 2022 PMID:36076757); and rare IgE asthma (de la Hoz 1991 PMID:1720290) and historical mandrake leaf adulteration (Jimenez-Mejias 1990 PMID:2087109) are documented.

Isolated soy-isoflavone capsules remain separate from culinary tofu.

Remains Unknown (Researched): No controlled human clinical trial shows raw walnuts worsen or ease anxiety severity. Both human whole-walnut RCTs measuring validated anxiety subscales were NULL between groups: Herselman 2022 (PMID:36432461, PMC9697272; n=80/60, 56 g/d raw walnuts x 16 wk) reported NO between-group difference on DASS-21 Anxiety (time p=0.0053) and no attenuation on POMS Tension-Anxiety (-4.10 walnut vs -4.94 control V2->V3), while Pribis 2016 (PMID:27792133, PMC5133056; n=49, 60 g/d baked walnut bread) reported NULL POMS Tension-Anxiety overall (11.2 vs 11.9, p=0.507), in men (p=0.117), and in women (12.6 vs 12.1, p=0.735). Bell 2025 (PMID:39924976) noted worse acute post-breakfast negative affect attributed to meal dislike, and moldy-walnut acute anxiety (Botha 2019, PMID:30088215) reflects Penicillium crustosum mycotoxin spoilage rather than sound raw walnuts. Safety caveats: major IgE-mediated tree-nut allergen capable of severe anaphylaxis with ~80% clinical walnut-pecan cross-reactivity and low eliciting threshold in dual-allergic individuals (Elizur 2020, PMID:31513892); acute tremorgenic neuromycotoxicosis (tremors, pain, incoordination, confusion, anxiety) reported after ingesting visibly moldy Penicillium crustosum-contaminated walnuts (Botha 2019, PMID:30088215); coughing/choking texture hazard with hard whole nuts in PD dysphagia (Parkinson's UK forum 2019, topic 20445); and high calorie/fat/protein density if consumed in large portions near levodopa dosing.

Remains Unknown (50): no controlled human trial has tested strained (Greek) yogurt on validated anxiety severity scales in Parkinson disease or clinical anxiety populations. Randomized trials testing conventional or probiotic yogurts on anxiety are null or use plain yogurt as the inert comparator: Mysonhimer 2024 (PMC11375456, n=62 crossover) was null on DASS-42 Anxiety (p=0.61) and PROMIS Anxiety (p=0.23); Mohammadi 2016 (PMID:25879690, n=70) found conventional yogurt control null on DASS (p=0.08); and Tillisch 2013 (PMC3839572, n=36 healthy women) measured only task-based fMRI emotional reactivity under a 4-strain fermented milk without clinical anxiety ratings. In PD, Lam 2026 (PMC13125604, n=61 DB-RCT) found 9-strain probiotic powder completely null on the Parkinson Anxiety Scale (+1.0, p=0.60), while Yang 2023 (PMID:37470081, n=128 PD: secondary HAMA -1.44) tested single-strain L. paracasei Shirota drink rather than strained yogurt.

Remains Unknown (50): no controlled clinical trial or Parkinson symptom cohort isolates strained yogurt on apathy severity. In Yang 2023 (PMID:37470081, n=128 PD), aggregate NMSS improved under single-strain L. paracasei Shirota fermented milk drink without reporting an isolated plain-yogurt effect on apathy severity, while Thriene 2026 (PMC13084677, n=110 healthy crossover) found 250 g/d plain yogurt transiently enriched S. thermophilus without changing systemic health markers. Large prospective dairy-epidemiology cohorts and meta-analyses (Olsson 2020 PMC7551962 n=81,915; Groninger 2024 PMC11646269 n=183,225 yogurt HR 1.03; Jiang 2014 PMID:24894826 yogurt RR 0.95; Yang 2026 PMID:41544344 yogurt null; Hughes 2017 PMC5496517 driven by skim/low-fat milk HR 1.39) show incident PD risk is null for yogurt and remote from symptom modification, while cross-sectional Mischley 2017 (PMC5610862) reports only a composite PRO-PD score.

Remains Unknown (50): no randomized trial isolates strained yogurt on attention impairment in Parkinson disease or older adults with cognitive impairment. Mysonhimer 2024 (PMC11375456, n=62 crossover RCT) found spatial cognitive reconstruction null (p=0.14) and a slight PROMIS cognitive interaction favoring heat-treated control (p=0.03), while Idrus 2026 (PMC13075031, n=966 Sydney Memory & Ageing prospective cohort) found NO association between yogurt intake and cognition or 5.2-year incident dementia. Papageorgiou 2024 (PMC11531444) notes insufficient interventional evidence for fermented dairy cognitive benefits in older adults, and Parkinson probiotic powder trial Lam 2026 (PMC13125604) provides no yogurt-specific estimate.

Remains Unknown (50): no controlled clinical trial or Parkinson symptom cohort isolates plain yogurt on bradykinesia severity. In Yang 2023 (PMID:37470081, n=128 PD), single-strain L. paracasei Shirota fermented milk drink showed no between-group MDS-UPDRS Part III motor advantage over acidified milk, and Zhou 2024 (PMID:38039960, 116-trial protein NMA) found no protein type including yogurt significantly improved gait speed or physical performance; dairy protein timing can acutely alter levodopa-mediated motor fluctuations via LNAA competition (Pimentel 2018, Brown 2023), captured specifically under daily OFF time (0873) rather than a standalone chronic effect on bradykinesia severity. Minimal directional signal toward easing constipation severity—opposing the frozen "worsens" hypothesis as Maybe False (50.005), calibrated consistently with Round 4 plain kefir (0931) while strictly separating plain yogurt from fortified fermented-milk trials. In Kinoshita 2021 (PMID:34030638, PMC8142513, n=961 RCT), 16 weeks of 112 mL/d yogurt fermented with starter species L. delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus OLL1073R-1 significantly prevented GSRS constipation worsening vs no-yogurt control (1.74->1.72 vs 1.76->1.84, p=0.03), and Yang 2008 (PMID:18985817, n=126 constipated women DB-RCT) reported higher stool frequency (4.1 vs 2.6/wk, p<0.01) and better defecation scores (p<0.01) for fermented milk with yogurt starter strains plus B. lactis DN-173010 vs acidified non-living milk. Within-arm symptom reductions also occurred under conventional plain yogurt in Mirghafourvand 2016 (PMC5294450, n=60 constipated pregnant women: 2.3->8.1/wk, matching probiotic yogurt p=0.872) and Magro 2014 (PMC4113128, n=47: Agachan 14.3->8.3, p<0.001), and Bui & Marco 2026 (PMC13161760, 37 fermented-dairy studies) identified zero GI worsening. Kept strictly at minimal_signal (50.005) rather than limited_clinical_link (51) because direct PD constipation DB-RCTs tested bundled probiotic+prebiotic-fiber fermented milk (Barichella 2016, PMID:27543643, n=120 PD, +1.1 CBMs/wk p=0.002; attribution_fit=remote) or single-strain L. paracasei Shirota fermented milk drink (Yang 2023, PMID:37470081, n=128 PD, Wexner -2.78; Cassani 2011, PMID:21587143, n=40 PD single-arm), NOT plain unfortified yogurt. Strongest opposing/null evidence preserved: Malpeli 2012 (PMID:23165580, n=83: plain control yogurt failed to shorten transit [+4.9%] vs synbiotic yogurt [-27.5%, p=0.023]), Magro 2014 (plain yogurt did not shorten colonic transit time or increase daily BMs vs synbiotic yogurt p=0.01), Mysonhimer 2024 (PMC11375456, n=62 crossover: live yogurt null on transit p=0.87 and stool frequency p=0.84), Mazlyn 2013 (PMID:23432408, n=90 LcS null at alpha=0.05), Tabbers 2011 (PMID:21606153, n=148 children null p=0.35), Aslam 2022 (PMID:33827333, n=1,241 cohort null), Park 2023 PD meta-analysis (PMC9990363: capsules outperformed fermented milk), and BDA 2025 guidelines (PMC12623288: no GRADE recommendation for plain yogurt). Clinical caveat: dairy yogurt protein can compete with daytime levodopa absorption in fluctuating PD.

Limited clinical link toward worsening daily OFF time—opposing the frozen "reduces" hypothesis as Maybe False (51), directly calibrated with Round 3 cow's milk (0718) and Round 4 kefir (0932). Four controlled direct-Parkinson clinical trials demonstrate that higher daytime dietary protein and elevated plasma large neutral amino acids (LNAAs) worsen daily OFF time: Barichella 2006 (PMID:16773618, n=18 PD crossover: total OFF 271 vs 164 min/d on standard vs protein-redistributed diet, p<0.0001), Tsui 1989 (PMID:2494567, n=10 PD blinded crossover), Carter 1989 (PMID:2648188, n=5 PD), and Eriksson 1988 (PMID:3135513).
